what_its_for: Obinutuzumab is a medicine used to treat certain types of blood cancers. It is approved to treat chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL, a type of blood cancer) and follicular lymphoma (FL, a type of slow-growing lymph node cancer). It works by helping your immune system find and destroy cancer cells.
how_to_take: Obinutuzumab is given as an intravenous (IV) infusion, meaning it goes directly into your vein through a needle or catheter. A nurse or doctor will give you this medicine at a clinic or hospital. You will NOT give this medicine to yourself at home. Each infusion can take several hours, so plan to spend most of the day at the clinic. You will be watched closely during and after each infusion for any reactions.
dosing: The dose and schedule your doctor prescribes will depend on your specific condition and body weight. A common schedule includes receiving infusions on certain days of the first treatment cycle, then once every 28 days for several more cycles. Your healthcare team will plan your exact schedule. Never change your dose or schedule without talking to your doctor first.
missed_dose: Because this medicine is given by healthcare professionals in a clinic, your appointments are carefully planned. If you need to reschedule or miss an appointment, call your doctor or clinic as soon as possible. Do not skip doses without letting your medical team know, as staying on schedule is very important for the medicine to work properly.
storage: Obinutuzumab is stored and prepared by healthcare professionals at the clinic or hospital. You do not need to store this medicine at home. If you are given any supplies related to your treatment, ask your healthcare team for specific storage instructions.
what_to_avoid: Avoid being around people who are sick or have infections, as this medicine can weaken your immune system and make it harder for you to fight infections. Do not receive live vaccines (such as the shingles vaccine Zostavax or the nasal flu vaccine) while on this treatment without asking your doctor first. Avoid aspirin and blood thinners unless your doctor approves them, as this medicine can lower your platelet counts and increase bleeding risk. Talk to your doctor before starting any new medicines, vitamins, or herbal supplements.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor or go to the emergency room right away if you experience any of the following: fever, chills, or signs of infection; difficulty breathing or shortness of breath; chest pain or fast heartbeat; severe dizziness or lightheadedness; unusual bruising or bleeding; swelling of the face, lips, or throat; sudden numbness, confusion, or vision changes; pain or burning when urinating; blisters or sores in your mouth; or any new or worsening symptoms. During your infusion, tell the nurse immediately if you feel flushed, itchy, short of breath, or unwell in any way.
when_it_works: Obinutuzumab does not work overnight. It may take several weeks to months of treatment before your doctors can see improvement through blood tests or scans. Every person responds differently. Your healthcare team will monitor your progress with regular tests throughout your treatment. Even if you feel the same or notice side effects, continue your appointments as scheduled unless your doctor tells you otherwise.
special_populations: Older adults (age 65 and over): Older patients may be more sensitive to side effects and will be monitored closely. Pregnant or breastfeeding women: This medicine can harm an unborn baby. Women who can become pregnant must use effective birth control during treatment and for 18 months after the last dose. Do not breastfeed during treatment and for 18 months after the last dose. Talk to your doctor immediately if you are pregnant or plan to become pregnant. People with hepatitis B: This medicine can cause hepatitis B to become active again, which can be life-threatening. Tell your doctor if you have ever had hepatitis B before starting treatment. Kidney or liver problems: Your doctor will review your medical history and may adjust your care plan if you have kidney or liver issues.
